Published online:
September 9, 2026

Geographic focus:
East Africa (Kenya, specifically Lamu; with references to Uganda, Tanzania, South Sudan, Nigeria)

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — references Nigeria refinery success, Kenya's 2013 refinery closure
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — groundbreaking ceremony end of September 2026
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — $15-16B project targeting 2030 completion, financing across 2025-2030, crude supply constraints

Synopsis:
Dangote Group plans to build a 700,000 bpd refinery in Lamu, Kenya, modelled on its Lagos success. The project faces three compounding risk categories: (1) feedstock — Kenya has no commercial crude output, regional pipeline infrastructure is unbuilt or rerouted elsewhere, leaving the refinery exposed to volatile seaborne markets with Middle East supply disruption risk; (2) financing — Dangote is simultaneously pursuing ~$40B in energy projects through 2030, making capital allocation highly strained; (3) infrastructure & ESG — Lamu port lacks oil storage terminals, heritage site proximity triggers environmental opposition. Analysts warn of "white elephant" risk if execution falters.
